paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.German: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Comparison" presents a side-by-side comparison of accuracy percentages between two reasoning methods—Vanilla CoT (light yellow bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark green bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 0 to 100 with major gridlines at 20% intervals. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. For each dataset, two adjacent bars show the performance of the two methods. On GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 92.5% accuracy, while TLDR (Ours) achieves 86.4%, indicated by a red label of “-1.6%”, suggesting a decrease. On MATH500, Vanilla CoT scores 86.4% and TLDR (Ours) scores 86.6%, marked with “+0.2%”, indicating a slight improvement. On AIME, both methods score 43.4%, with a “-0.1%” label, implying near-identical performance. On AMC, Vanilla CoT scores 79.6% and TLDR (Ours) scores 83.5%, marked with “+3.9%”, showing a notable improvement. The bars are not sorted by height, and the chart visually emphasizes the relative change in accuracy via small red labels above each pair of bars. The caption notes that the TLDR method consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales, though generation length is not visually represented in this chart.
